results.fact: Timing of the Flypaper Pass snow finger
results.evidence: Two outside accounts agree the Flypaper Pass snow finger is best climbed in spring or early summer, and a mid-July report found the chutes badly melted out with exposed ice, so the approach and waypoint text are correct as written. What would need to change is the route's own season window and August 'optimal' rating (and the itinerary cal), but no source gives a season for this undocumented spire itself; settling it needs a sourced best window for the whole Anderson's Thumb trip (e.g. a trip report or route page stating the months) before re-rating July/August.

results.fact: Descent line off the summit block
results.evidence: One outside guide says its party descended the left side of the peak, which was much easier than the rock scramble up, then retraced the trail. Other accounts found (search excerpts) describe parties simply reversing the ascent line, and the trail-association page only warns to take care descending. The row itself is split three fields (descent_text, climbing_route[2], approach) against three (itinerary note, schedule 'Reverse the route', descent). A second independent source explicitly recommending the left/west-side downclimb over the ascent gully would settle it.

The only stale copy is in bivy[0].notes (Heart o' the Hills campground, a staging camp not on the route). The trail-association page gives 700 ft of gain in 0.6 mile for the Switchback Trail, matching beta and approach. No bivy patch is written per the camping clean-up rule; the camp card's '1,000 ft' should be corrected in that pass.

season is the outer window (late Jun-Sep) and the best window (mid/late July-September) sits inside it; best_season explicitly addresses June-early July parties with residual snow and an ice axe, and June is rated risky rather than closed.

results.fact: Direction of the Sol Duc River Trail
results.correct_value: upriver (east) from the trailhead to the Appleton Pass junction at 4.9 mi
results.evidence: The trail-association page puts the Appleton Pass junction 4.9 miles up the Sol Duc River Trail, heading inland/upriver from the road end; a second trail guide describes hiking above the Sol Duc River past the falls and then staying left onto the Appleton Pass Trail. The Sol Duc flows northwest here, so upriver is east/southeast, matching the row's approach ('upriver') and the waypoint pins.

patches.replace: Follow the Sol Duc River Trail upriver (east) about 4.9 miles

results.fact: Which fork at the Appleton Pass junction
results.correct_value: Appleton Pass Trail is the left fork; the right fork crosses the Sol Duc River on a footlog toward Sol Duc Park
results.evidence: The trail-association page says to stay right at the 4.9-mile Appleton Pass junction to continue on the Sol Duc River Trail, which crosses the river on a footlog. A second guide says to stay left onto the Appleton Pass Trail. The waypoint note had the river crossing and the right fork on the Appleton side.

results.fact: Boston Charlie's Camp elevation vs gain to summit
results.evidence: USGS 3DEP ground elevation at the mapped Boston Charlie's Camp point is ~5,543 ft (matching bivy[3].elev), which leaves only ~1,450 ft to the 6,995 ft summit; but the widely repeated route description says the southwest ridge gains 2,000 ft in under a mile from the camp, and the same figure is also in pitch_detail[3].notes (not only the bivy card). No second source gives either the camp's elevation or a different gain figure, so neither copy is changed; a topo-derived camp elevation from a second source, or a trip report stating the camp-to-summit gain, would settle it.

results.correct_value: ~13 mi applies to Boston Charlie's Camp only; Cat Basin is several miles closer
results.evidence: The Cat Basin primitive trail leaves the High Divide junction (8.4 mi from the trailhead) and runs east toward Cat Basin and Appleton Pass; an outside traverse account puts Cat Peak about 3 miles from Heart Lake, and another party reached Cat Basin camp on day one and crossed the Catwalk only on the summit day, so Cat Basin is well short of Boston Charlie's. Removing Cat Basin from the '13 miles' sentence makes the approach agree with the waypoints.

results.correct_value: Deer Lake junction under a mile in (at the falls bridge); Heart Lake ~7 mi beyond it (~8 mi from the trailhead)
results.evidence: Trail guides put Sol Duc Falls at 0.8 mi and the Deer Lake Trail leaving across the falls bridge, with Deer Lake itself about 3.4 mi out at ~3,527 ft on a side trail; Heart Lake is 7.85-8.0 mi from the trailhead. results.fact: Deer Lake Trail junction pin sits on Deer Lake
results.evidence: waypoints[2] is named and described as the junction on the Sol Duc River Trail, but its coordinates are on Deer Lake itself (ground elevation 3,525 ft, and 3.7 mi matches the lake's distance), an off-route side trail. The real junction is at the Sol Duc Falls bridge, under a mile in. Moving the pin is out of scope; settle by relocating the pin to the falls bridge and then setting elev (~1,950 ft) and distMi (~0.8-0.9).
